S1-R1: The Inventory list shows two tabs, Active and Inactive.
S1-R2: Active is the selected tab when the page opens.
S1-R3: The Active tab lists only parts that are active.
S1-R4: The Inactive tab lists only parts that are inactive.
S1-R5: Every part that exists when this feature is released is active.
S1-R6: Switching tabs clears any rows the user had selected.
S1-R7: Search, filters and sort work the same way on both tabs.
S1-N1: If there are no inactive parts, the Inactive tab displays an empty state (no parts listed).
S2-R1: Bulk deactivation is a mode. The user turns it on from the Inventory actions menu, the three-dot button in the toolbar that already holds Cycle count and Export.
S2-R2: That menu entry reads "Deactivate parts" while the Active tab is showing and "Activate parts" while the Inactive tab is showing. It is one entry, never both, and it sits between Cycle count and Export.
S2-R3: Outside the mode the Inventory list has no checkbox column and no row actions, and a row click opens the part. None of that changes.
S2-R4: Turning the mode on adds a checkbox column 44px wide at the left of the table and scrolls the table back to its left edge so the column is in view.
S2-R5: While the mode is on, clicking anywhere on a row ticks or unticks that row instead of opening the part.
S2-R6: The checkbox in the header ticks or clears every row currently loaded in the list.
S2-R7: While the mode is on, the bulk bar spans the full width of the list directly under the Active and Inactive tabs, and the search and filter row moves down beneath it. The bar is near-black (#121926) with white text in the light theme and white with near-black text in the dark theme, with 8px rounded corners.
S2-R7a: From left to right the bar shows: the number of ticked rows in a round badge followed by the word "selected", a thin divider, and a blue button reading "Deactivate" on the Active tab or "Activate" on the Inactive tab. The number updates as the user ticks.
S2-R8: That button is disabled while no row is ticked. Hovering it then shows "Tick the parts to deactivate" on the Active tab and "Tick the parts to activate" on the Inactive tab.
S2-R9: An X button sits at the right end of the bar. Hovering it shows "Clear selection", which is also its screen reader label. It leaves the mode, clears the selection and returns the toolbar to its normal state.
S2-R10: Search, the filter bar, sorting and paging all keep working while the mode is on, the same as they do in Cycle count.
S2-R11: When the user confirms the action, every ticked part becomes inactive.
S2-R12: The parts that were deactivated leave the Active tab without the user reloading the page.
S2-R13: The parts that were deactivated appear on the Inactive tab.
S2-R14: When every ticked part changes successfully, the mode is left and the selection is cleared.
S2-R15: When some parts fail, the mode stays on and the selection keeps only the parts that failed.
S2-R16: Switching between the Active and Inactive tabs leaves the mode and clears the selection.
S2-R17: A single part can also be deactivated from its edit dialog, without entering the mode. That control is labelled "Deactivate" on an active part and "Activate" on an inactive one.
S2-R18: That control sits at the left end of the dialog footer, apart from Delete and Save, which stay at the right. It is blue text with no border and no fill, in both states.
S2-N1: With nothing ticked the Deactivate button is visible but disabled, so the confirmation cannot be opened.
S2-N2: Outside the mode there is no checkbox column, so no part can be ticked from the default list.
S2-E1: If a part being set inactive sits on an open work order, the change still goes through.
S2-E2: That part stays on the open work order.
S2-E3: The part's work order and invoice history is not changed. The status change itself is recorded in the part's own history, per Story 10.
S2-E4: Cycle count and bulk status cannot both be on. While Cycle count is running the actions menu is replaced by the count controls, so there is no way to reach the bulk status entry until the count is saved or discarded.
S3-R1: Reactivation uses the same mode as Story 2. On the Inactive tab the actions menu entry reads "Activate parts" and turning it on shows the same checkbox column and the same bulk bar.
S3-R2: The bulk bar button reads "Activate". It is the same blue as "Deactivate" on the Active tab.
S3-R5: S2-R3 through S2-R10 and S2-R14 through S2-R18 apply on the Inactive tab exactly as they do on the Active tab, with the wording changed from deactivate to activate.
S3-R3: When the user confirms the action, all selected parts are moved to active and removed from the Inactive tab immediately, no page refresh required.
S3-R4: The reactivated parts appear in the Active tab.
S3-N1: With nothing ticked the Activate button is visible but disabled.
S4-R1: The New Inventory Part dialog contains a "Track quantities and cost of goods" toggle, defaulting to ON.
S4-R2: The toggle has no tooltip, no info icon and no helper text.
S4-R3: When the user turns the toggle OFF, the Min and Max fields are hidden.
S4-R4: When the toggle is OFF, the bin location section remains visible but is optional, the user may assign a bin for physical reference without it being required to save.
S4-R5: When the toggle is ON, at least one bin location must be assigned and marked as default before the part can be saved.
S4-R6: The toggle sits in its own section headed "Inventory tracking", below Average Cost, Sell Price and Core Charge and above Tags. The heading is plain text in the same style as the "Inventory" heading over the bin locations, with no box around the section. Min and Max sit inside the section, under the toggle.
S4-R7: On successful save, untracked parts appear in the Inventory list with "Not Tracked" displayed in the Total Quantity column instead of a quantity badge.
S4-N1: If the user attempts to save a tracked part with no bin location assigned, the system displays: "At least one bin must be provided."
S4-N2: If the user assigns bin locations but none is marked as the default, the system displays: "At least one bin must be marked as default."
S5-R1: The "Track quantities and cost of goods" toggle is enabled in edit mode, the user can change the tracking state of an existing part.
S5-R2: When the user turns tracking on and the part has no bin location, the system gives it the workplace's default bin location.
S5-R3: That bin location is created with a quantity of zero.
S5-R4: That bin location is marked as the default bin.
S5-R5: When the user turns tracking on and the part has bin locations but none is the default, the system marks the first one as the default.
S5-R6: When the user turns tracking off, the Min and Max fields are hidden.
S5-R7: When the user turns tracking off, the Min and Max values are cleared on save.
S5-R8: After a successful save, the Total Quantity column shows the new tracking state without the user reloading the page.
S5-N1: If the user turns tracking ON but removes all bin locations before saving, the system displays: "At least one bin must be provided."
S5-E1: If the user turns tracking off on a part that holds more than zero on hand, a confirmation appears before anything changes.
S5-E2: The confirmation states how many units the part currently holds.
S5-E3: The confirmation states that turning tracking off will clear the quantity in every bin location.
S5-E4: The confirmation is the application's standard confirmation dialog, the same one every other destructive action in the product uses. It carries a title, the message, a Cancel and a confirm button, and nothing else. There is no field to type into and nothing to transcribe: the confirm button is available as soon as the dialog opens.
S5-E4a: The confirm button reads Disable tracking and is styled as a destructive action. Cancel sits beside it, in the position the standard dialog puts it.
S5-E5: On confirmation, every bin quantity for that part is set to zero.
S5-E6: On confirmation, the part is saved as untracked.
S5-E7: If the user cancels, the toggle returns to on.
S5-E8: If the user cancels, nothing about the part is changed.
S5-E9: If the user turns tracking off on a part holding zero, no confirmation appears and the toggle changes straight away.
S6-R1: Typing "not tracked" (or any partial match such as "not", "tracked") in the global search field returns only untracked parts.
S6-R2: Typing other search terms does not surface untracked parts via their tracking state, only part number, name, tags, and other standard fields drive matches.
S6-R3: The Total Quantity column can be sorted.
S6-R4: When that column is sorted, untracked parts sit below every tracked part.
S6-R5: Untracked parts stay below tracked parts in both sort directions.
S6-R6: Tracked parts sort against each other by quantity.
S6-R7: Within the tracked group, parts holding the same quantity are then ordered by part name, A to Z.
S6-R8: Within the untracked group, parts are ordered by part name, A to Z.
S6-N1: If there are no untracked parts, searching "not tracked" returns an empty result set.
S7-R1: The New Inventory Part dialog has a free-text Part Number field.
S7-R2: The dialog has a free-text Part Name field.
S7-R3: The dialog has no part library selector and no part library lookup step.
S7-R4: On save, the system searches the part library for an entry with the part number the user typed.
S7-R5: The search ignores upper and lower case.
S7-R6: The search also ignores hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces in the part number.
S7-R7: If exactly one entry matches, the new part is linked to that entry.
S7-R8: If no entry matches, the system creates a new part library entry and links the part to it.
S7-R9: If more than one entry matches, the system lists the matching entries and the user chooses one.
S7-R10: The user is not told about the part library when exactly one entry matches or when none matches.
S7-R11: Parts created before this feature keep working with the part library entry they already have.
S7-N3: If either field is empty on save, the system shows an error on that field and does not save.
S8-R1: Deactivating a part requires the user to have the 'Part Library & Inventory - Delete' permission enabled.
S8-R2: Activating a part requires that same setting.
S8-R3: A user without that setting does not see the "Deactivate parts" entry in the Inventory actions menu, so there is no way for them to enter the mode from the Active tab.
S8-R4: The same user does not see the "Activate parts" entry on the Inactive tab.
S8-R15: The actions menu itself, and its Cycle count and Export entries, are unaffected by that setting. Only the bulk status entry is gated.
S8-R16: That same user does not see the Deactivate or Activate control in the part edit dialog.
S8-R5: Creating a part with tracking turned off requires that same setting.
S8-R6: Changing an existing part from tracked to untracked requires that same setting.
S8-R7: Changing an existing part from untracked to tracked requires that same setting.
S8-R8: A user without that setting still sees the tracking toggle when editing a part.
S8-R9: For that user the tracking toggle is disabled, so they can read the current state but cannot change it.
S8-R10: Creating a tracked part needs only the 'Part Library & Inventory - Create & Edit' permission.
S8-R11: Editing pricing, editing bin quantities and viewing the inventory list are unchanged by this spec.
S8-R12: Owner, Administrator and Parts Manager have the delete-level setting enabled by default.
S8-R13: Parts Technician, Technician, Service Advisor, Service Manager, Foreman and Office User do not have it enabled by default.
S8-R14: A custom role has only the settings that were explicitly granted to it.
S8-N1: If a user without the delete-level setting tries to save an untracked part by any route, including a direct call to the system, the request is refused with an access denied error.
S8-N2: If such a user tries to change a part's tracking state by any route, the request is refused with an access denied error.
S8-N3: If such a user tries to set a part active or inactive by any route, the request is refused with an access denied error.
S9-R1: Part lookup on a work order line does not return inactive parts.
S9-R2: Part lookup on an estimate line does not return inactive parts.
S9-R3: Technician charge-out part selection does not return inactive parts.
S9-R4: Part lookup on a standalone invoice line does not return inactive parts.
S9-R5: Part lookup on a purchase order line does not return inactive parts.
S9-R6: Part lookup on a vendor bill line does not return inactive parts.
S9-R7: Barcode and scan based part lookup does not return inactive parts.
S9-R8: Part lookup for a parts return does not return inactive parts.
S9-R9: Part lookup for a part sale credit does not return inactive parts.
S9-R13: Part lookup on a part sale line does not return inactive parts.
S9-R10: Inactive parts are listed only on the Inactive tab, which is what distinguishes them from active parts.
S9-R11: Opening a retired part for editing shows a grey "Inactive" badge beside the Part Number label, per S13-R2.
S9-N1: A user who can view the inventory list can open the Inactive tab.
S9-N2: Seeing inactive parts needs no extra permission.
S9-N3: Only changing a part's status needs the delete-level parts permission.
S9-N4: A user who cannot view the inventory list at all sees neither tab.
S9-E1: If a part is set inactive while it already sits on an open work order or estimate, the existing line stays and its totals keep calculating.
S9-E2: The user can still change the quantity, price and line notes on an existing line whose part has since become inactive.
S9-E3: The user cannot swap another line onto an inactive part through normal lookup.
S9-E4: Converting a work order to an invoice succeeds when a line references a part that became inactive after it was added.
S9-E5: Completed and invoiced work orders that reference inactive parts stay viewable, printable and reportable.
S9-E6: Reopening a completed work order does not reactivate any inactive part on it.
S9-E7: Viewing a line whose part is now inactive shows an indication that the part is inactive.
S10-R1: Setting a part inactive shows a confirmation before it is applied. It is the application's standard confirmation dialog, with no field to type into.
S10-R2: The confirmation states that the part will be hidden from operational lookup.
S10-R3: The confirmation states that historical records are not changed.
S10-R4: When the action covers more than one part, the confirmation states how many parts are selected.
S10-R5: After a bulk status change, the system shows how many parts succeeded.
S10-R6: After a bulk status change, the system shows how many parts failed.
S10-R7: For each part that failed, the system names the part and the reason.
S10-R8: Every status change records which user made it.
S10-R9: Every status change records the date and time it was made.
S10-R10: The user can add an optional note when changing a status.
S10-R11: A note can be at most 255 characters.
S10-R12: If a note is longer than 255 characters, the change is refused with the message "A note cannot be longer than 255 characters."
S10-R13: Leaving the note empty is allowed and records no note.
S10-R14: The part record shows its current status as a badge beside the Part Number label, per S13-R2.
S10-R15: Every status change is written to that part's history as its own entry. A part that is deactivated and later reactivated keeps both entries, each with its own note.
S10-R16: The history entry is typed "Deactivated" for a deactivation and "Activated" for a reactivation.
S10-R17: When the user gave a note, the entry reads "Deactivated | Reason: {note}". When the note was left empty it reads "Deactivated" and nothing else, with no trailing separator.
S10-R18: The status note held on the part record itself is the most recent one only. The history is the record of every change, and the two are not expected to agree once a part has changed status more than once.
S10-R19: A bulk change over forty parts writes forty history entries, one per part, each carrying the same note.
S10-R20: The confirmation raised from a selection on the list is titled "Deactivate parts?" or "Activate parts?". The confirmation raised from one part's edit dialog is titled "Deactivate part?" or "Activate part?".
S10-R21: The confirmation raised from a selection opens with "{n} parts selected.", or "1 part selected." for one. The confirmation raised from one part's edit dialog opens with that part's number followed by its name.
S10-R22: For a deactivation raised from a selection, the confirmation states, in this order: "These parts won't show up when adding parts to work orders, estimates, part sales or purchase orders.", "Existing records that use them stay as they are.", and "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected." When exactly one part is selected the lines read "This part won't show up ..." and "Existing records that use it stay as they are."
S10-R22a: For a deactivation raised from one part's edit dialog, the confirmation states, in this order: "This part won't show up when adding parts to work orders, estimates, part sales or purchase orders.", "Existing records that use it stay as they are.", and "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected."
S10-R23: For a reactivation raised from one part's edit dialog, the confirmation states "This part can be added to new work again." and nothing further. Raised from a selection it states "These parts can be added to new work again." (or "This part ..." for one) followed by "Existing records that use them stay as they are." Reactivating puts a part back in part lookup and has no other effect, so there is nothing else to rule out.
S10-R24: The note field is labelled "Note (optional)" and stops accepting input at 255 characters, so S10-R12 applies to requests that do not come from the dialog.
S10-R25: Deactivating a single part from the part edit dialog takes the same permission, sends to the same endpoint, offers the same note field and writes the same history entry as a bulk change of one. Only the title and the opening line differ, naming the part instead of a count, per S10-R20 and S10-R21.
S10-R26: The Part History table keeps the same column layout whatever an entry says. A short entry such as "Deactivated" does not widen the Staff, Date or Time columns, and the Event column continues to take the remaining width.
S10-R27: A status change appears in Part History with the same Staff, Date and Time columns as every other event, and is searchable from the Part History search like any other entry.
S10-R28: In every confirmation the confirm button is red for a deactivation and blue for a reactivation, from either entry point. Cancel is plain text to its left.
S10-R29: The "Existing records that use ..." line is set in medium weight wherever it appears. The "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected." line is set in grey. Every other line is regular weight in the default text color.
S10-N1: If the user cancels the confirmation, no part changes status.
S10-N2: If every part in a bulk change fails, the list stays on screen and the selection is kept so the user can retry.
S10-N3: If a status change is sent with no parts selected, it is refused with the message "Select at least one part."
S11-R1: The Part Library page has no control that creates a library entry. The "New Catalog Part" button is removed from its toolbar.
S11-R2: No dialog for creating a library entry is reachable from the Part Library page.
S11-R3: Clicking a row opens that library part's detail page, where the entry can still be edited and deleted. That is unchanged.
S11-R4: Row selection on the Part Library list and its bulk "Set category" action are unchanged.
S11-R5: Search, filtering, sorting and the column set on the Part Library list are unchanged.
S11-R6: Every new library entry is created by find-or-create against a part number. The routes that do so are: creating an inventory part (S7-R8), a part request, a delivery receipt, a core charge, the parts CSV import, and the public API create endpoint.
S11-R7: Because the toolbar no longer holds a create control, a user with the create-and-edit setting and a user without it see the same Part Library toolbar.
S11-N1: There is no route in the interface that produces a library entry with no inventory part, part request, delivery receipt, core charge or import row behind it.
S11-E1: Library entries that already exist stay in the list, including the ones nothing references. This spec does not delete or hide them.
S11-E2: An entry with no inventory part behind it is still editable from its detail page, and is still the entry S7-R7 links to when someone later creates a part with that number.
S11-E3: The public API create endpoint is a separate integration surface and is not changed by S11-R1.
S12-R1: The Parts left menu entry reads Part Library. It read Catalog.
S12-R2: The page title on that screen reads Part Library. It read Catalog.
S12-R3: The dialog for editing a library entry is titled Edit Library Part. It was titled Edit Catalog Part. The create title, New Catalog Part, disappears with the control itself per S11-R1.
S12-R4: The failure message when saving a library entry reads Failed to save library part. It read Failed to save catalog part.
S12-R5: The success message when deleting a library entry reads Library part deleted successfully. It read Catalog part deleted successfully.
S12-R6: On Administration -> Roles & Permissions -> Edit Role, the permission group is titled Part Library and Inventory. It was titled Catalog and Inventory.
S12-R7: That group's description reads Manage the parts library and inventory levels. It read Manage the parts catalog and inventory levels.
S12-R8: The Parts Department card description above that group reads Manage parts inventory, part library, sales, and vendor operations. It read Manage parts inventory, catalog, sales, and vendor operations.
S12-R9: The three permission labels read Part Library & Inventory - View, Part Library & Inventory - Create & Edit and Part Library & Inventory - Delete. They read Catalog & Inventory - View, Catalog & Inventory - Create & Edit and Catalog & Inventory - Delete.
S12-R10: A part lookup result that comes from the shared list shows its source as Part Library. It showed Catalog.
S12-N1: No permission is added, removed or re-keyed. Every user's access on the day of release is identical to the day before.
S12-N2: The address of the Part Library page does not change, so an existing bookmark or saved link still resolves.
S12-N3: No stored data is renamed. The change is confined to text a user reads on screen.
S13-R1: In the Edit Inventory Part dialog the part number is shown as text, not as an input. The top of the dialog is a label row reading "Part Number" followed by the status badge, and under it the part number in bold 18px text with an edit button beside it.
S13-R2: The status badge is a rounded pill. It reads "Active" in green (#16833c on a light green fill) on an active part and "Inactive" in grey (#475467 on a light grey fill) on an inactive one.
S13-R3: The edit button is a blue square-and-pen icon, 24px square. It has no tooltip. Its screen reader label is "Edit part number". Its vertical center lines up with the vertical center of the part number.
S13-R4: Clicking the edit button replaces the label row and the number with a "Part Number" field holding the current number, focused, and two 40px square buttons to its right: an X ("Cancel") and a blue check ("Confirm").
S13-R5: Under the field the dialog shows "Enter to apply, Esc to cancel. Saved with the rest of the part."
S13-R6: The check, or Enter, puts the typed number back into the label, with leading and trailing spaces removed. Nothing is saved at this point.
S13-R7: The X, or Esc, discards the typed number and shows the number the part had.
S13-R8: Save sends the part number with the rest of the part. If the field is still open when the user presses Save, the typed number is applied first rather than dropped.
S13-R9: Saving a new number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every work order, invoice and purchase order line that uses it. The part's own Part Library entry is renamed with it. No new Part Library entry is created.
S13-R10: Saving with the number unchanged changes nothing about the number or the Part Library entry.
S13-R11: Creating a part is unchanged. The New Inventory Part dialog keeps the plain Part Number field of Story 7.
S13-R12: A Part Library entry is shared by every location in the organization, so the new number applies at every location that stocks the part, not only the one where it was edited.
S13-R13: While the Part Number field is open, if at least one other location stocks the same Part Library entry, the dialog shows "This also changes the part number at {n} other locations." under the hint, or "This also changes the part number at 1 other location." for one. Parts at those locations count whether they are active or inactive. When no other location stocks it, nothing extra is shown.
S13-R14: Work orders, estimates, invoices, part sales, purchase orders, receipts and returns keep the part number they were saved with. Reports, the Inventory list and Part History show the new number.
S13-N1: If another part in the shop's Part Library already has the typed number, the save is refused, the dialog stays open, and the system shows "Part number {number} already belongs to another part in the Part Library." The match ignores upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces, the same way S7-R5 and S7-R6 do.
S13-N2: If the field is empty, the check and Enter do nothing and the field shows "Part number is a required field".
S13-N3: If an empty part number reaches the system by any other route, the save is refused with "Part number is required."
